signals.title: USD/JPY — Intervention Risk + Geopolitical Conflict
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 160.19, clearing the 160.00 threshold that historically triggers BoJ/MoF verbal warnings and market-intervention watch. The move is fueled by the US-Iran conflict escalation, with G20 statements flagging Strait of Hormuz maritime disruptions as a primary supply-chain risk. While a 275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage supports the bid, the 25d Risk Reversal at -1.79 signals a heavy put skew as the options market pays up for downside protection against a policy-forced reversal. JPY COT LF net short of -81,619 (pctl 9) confirms that positioning remains heavily stretched to the short side, leaving little room for error if intervention occurs. Trade bias: Neutral/Bearish USD/JPY; 160.00 level triggers heightened intervention risk despite carry support. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting — hike bias priced. Risk: conflict escalation drives broad risk-off JPY safe-haven flows, bypassing the carry-trade logic.

signals.title: NZD/USD — G10 Bilateral Theme + RBNZ Hike Bias
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5895 as the G10 scorecard flags a 1.167% spread between the week's leader (USD +0.658%) and laggard (NZD -0.509%). RBNZ holds at 2.5%. NZD positioning is now at its most extreme short level of the year (z -2.60), making it highly sensitive to a hawkish delivery. Price is currently testing the SMA200 at 0.5853 and the SMA20 at 0.5912; a hold above the 200-day average keeps the squeeze potential alive. Trade bias: Bullish NZD/USD; extreme spec shorting faces a hawkish RBNZ repricing risk. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep — hike bias priced. Risk: RBNZ holds at 2.5% and hike pricing fades, validating the record spec short.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Retail Divergence + Commodity Risk
signals.text: AUD/USD is trading at 0.7148, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.6978–0.7114). Institutional positioning shows AUD LF net long at +53,578 (pctl 95), marking a crowded institutional long at the upper decile of its 52-week range. This contrasts sharply with retail sentiment, which is 85% short, creating a classic retail-vs-institutional divergence at extreme levels. While the 60bp AUD carry premium supports the pair, headlines regarding the Middle East conflict are weighing on high-beta currencies as oil prices rise. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; institutional-retail divergence favors current trend but crowded positioning limits near-term gains. Catalyst: Australian GDP data. Risk: US-Iran conflict escalation triggers a move into USD-cash, liquidating commodity-linked longs.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Volatility Premium
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3515, currently positioned below its SMA20 (1.3549) but above its SMA50/200 cluster near 1.3440. The options market is pricing a significant risk premium, with GBP/USD 1M ATM IV at 11.0% vs HV30 of 5.0%, resulting in a +6.0% VRP. This elevated premium suggests that despite neutral carry (0bp spread vs Fed), the market is aggressively hedging against upcoming policy risk. Speculative positioning remains net long +56,839 (pctl 96, z +1.58), which aligns with the institutional demand for protection. Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD; high vol premium makes directional plays expensive ahead of CB meetings. Catalyst: next BoE meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) — market bias Hold. Risk: GBP/USD closes through the SMA50/200 cluster at 1.3436/1.3443, shifting the technical regime to bearish.
